text: Core systems are up. Barely.
The cache is thin, the tanks are draining, and nobody has told the people what happens next. That would be you.
Asleep, mostly. Those who could still walk are waiting to see if you keep the lights on.
I would start there.
A hub, a handful of scrap, and a grid that will not carry much.
Power first. Everything else wants it.
The radar hums. Somewhere beyond the walls, the wastes wait.
The tanks are filling and the pantry is not shrinking. I had stopped expecting that.
People are starting to notice. They are looking at the walls differently.
A second site, with its own grid and its own stores. We are no longer one fortress, we are a network.
Keep the roads open. They will be asked to carry more than anyone planned.
The array is standing. All it wants now is power and time.
Whatever answers, we should be ready for it.
Carrier detected. We are listening.
Your message crossed the wastes. Others heard it too.
There is a harbour on the far side. It trades with anyone who has something worth trading.
A market, then. We will need goods that are worth more than scrap.
And we will need to decide who we deal with.
Open hands, then. They will remember who paid well.
A wise instinct. Favours are a currency here, and they are not cheap to earn back.
You have been filling orders. Good. Few do.
The foundries run on tool steel and patience. Bring us the first, and we will teach you the second.
We keep the valleys alive, one jar at a time.
If you can keep our shelves stocked, we can keep your people well.
Meridian moves anything, anywhere, on schedule.
Finished goods by the crate, and we will make sure it gets where it is going.
Word has spread. The factions know your name now, and someone has sent plans for something far bigger than a beacon.
A staging platform and a catapult on the outer ring, and a command center at the harbour. Orbit, if we can afford it.
The station is in orbit. Orbital Command is open: storage, links to the Core, and one dropship.
Below, the anomalies are opening ground nobody has seen. It will not stay open.
Higher now. Closer.
The recovery rig found a data fragment. One fragment is not enough to read anything. Gather more and the records can be assembled into a packet.
A Data screen has opened on your terminal. Look for more data sites in the territories.
More. Keep looking.

mail.subject: Lights on
body: The grid is holding. It is not much, but it is ours.
Scrap next. Everything we build is paid for in it.

mail.subject: A convoy at the gate
body: Traders pass on a schedule. They pay for surplus and they sell what we cannot make.
Set your terms before they arrive. They will not wait.

mail.subject: Concentrated power
body: The first power cell came off the line today. Dense, quiet, and worth more than the rest of the cache together.

mail.subject: You are not alone
body: Every order you fill is heard further than you think.
There are others like you. In time, you may meet them.

mail.subject: A seat at the table
body: You have earned a name in the foundries. That does not happen often.
There will be work for you, if you want it.

mail.subject: Seeds for the road
body: Come and see what grows when it is tended properly.

mail.subject: Preferred routing
body: Your crates arrive on time and in one piece. We notice.
Consider yourself on our short list.

mail.subject: Payload ready
body: The payload is complete and the staging platform has stood down. The catapult is waiting for your word, and a name for the station.

mail.subject: Samples
body: The dropship brought back something the colony has never had. The orbital foundry can work it, two kinds at a time.
Whatever it makes may be worth bringing back down. The colony's buildings were laid out to grow taller than they are.
